chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAbbās, from Abī Hammām, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
"There is no harm in his performing the prayer of the night and the day with one tayammum so long as he does not incur hadath or find water."

Then he said—may Allah the Exalted support him: Whoever lacks water should not perform tayammum until the time of the prayer enters. Then he should seek it in front of him, to his right, and to his left, to the measure of two arrow-shots from every direction if the land is level; and if it is rugged, he should seek it in every direction to the measure of one arrow-shot. If he does not find it, then let him perform tayammum at the end of the prayer time when he has despaired of it, and then pray with the tayammum that we have explained.

What has passed earlier indicates the obligation of seeking water to the extent estimated as two arrow-shots when fear has ceased, and that when fear is present, seeking is not obligatory; and this confirms that.

key_terms.الْإِيَاسِ: despair of finding water after searching
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water required for ritual purification when available
key_terms.تَيَمُّمٍ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl when water is unavailable
key_terms.رَمْيَةِ سَهْمَيْنِ: the distance of two arrow-shots, used here as a measure for searching
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed during the night
key_terms.وَقْتُ الصَّلَاةِ: the legally designated time for performing the prayer
key_terms.يُحْدِثْ: to incur ritual impurity that invalidates the prior state of purification

ai.seo_question: When should a person perform tayammum, and how far must they search for water before doing so?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling on tayammum, stating that one tayammum may suffice for multiple prayers of the night and day so long as it is not invalidated by hadath or by finding water. It also explains that a person missing water should wait until prayer time begins, search for water within a defined range depending on the terrain, and only then perform tayammum near the end of the prayer time if still unable to find water.
